deep_dive_html:
The Peril of Unrestricted Personal Liability

For dental practitioners, the personal guarantee is often the most dangerous instrument in a commercial lease. While landlords view these guarantees as essential security, an unmitigated guarantee effectively pierces the corporate veil, stripping away the protections of your LLC or Professional Corporation. In an unlimited guarantee, you are not merely guaranteeing the rent; you are tethering your personal estate—including your home, bank accounts, and retirement assets—to the entire duration of the lease term, regardless of whether the practice remains profitable or even operational.

Landlords exploit this by drafting "unconditional and irrevocable" language that remains in effect even if the practice undergoes a change in ownership or a significant downturn in patient volume. This creates a catastrophic risk profile where a business failure becomes a personal financial ruin.

Implementing Market-Standard Protections

An elite negotiation strategy focuses on limiting the scope and duration of the guarantee. You should never accept a "full-term" guarantee without specific, enforceable limitations. The goal is to transition from a permanent liability to a finite, manageable obligation.

  • Burn-Off Provisions: Negotiate a clause where the personal guarantee automatically expires after a set period, such as the first 36 or 48 months of the lease term, provided the tenant is not in default.
  • The "Good Guy" Clause: This is the gold standard for practitioners. It limits your personal liability to the period during which you occupy the premises and remain in compliance with the lease, terminating your obligation upon the surrender of the space and payment of all arrears.
  • Liability Caps: If a burn-off is rejected, insist on a hard cap on the total amount of the guarantee, often expressed as a specific number of months of base rent.

Identifying these predatory clauses requires a forensic review of the "Guaranty" exhibit, which is often overlooked during the excitement of a new build-out.
